page: Amazon Web Services r8i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores running at clock frequencies up to 3.9 GHz. Its memory subsystem consists of 384 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The CPU topology incorporates a 480 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512, AMX tile, and AMX int8 execution units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong in-memory throughput and computational capabilities. The platform achieves a PassMark CPU score of 69,028.35 and registers 87.47 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 3,860.19 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 192.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Geekbench testing yields a multi-core score of 19,625.0, with top-decile performance in image processing (19,927.0) and text processing (2,840.0). Integrated AMX units also support efficient CPU-based inference, processing 346.76 text generation tokens per second on a 135M model and 28.14 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The instance delivers a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides no bundled local instance storage, requiring remote storage volumes for stateful persistence. Because discrete GPUs are absent, accelerated model training is unsupported. However, the generous DDR5 allocation and cache density offer qualitative cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads without overpaying for excessive compute scale. The r8i.12xlarge is suited for in-memory key-value stores, distributed caches, relational databases, data analytics, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based server featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 384 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory alongside an expansive 480 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 instructions. Network bandwidth is rated at a 22 Gbps baseline, and the server contains no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight strong in-memory and computational efficiency, including 87.47 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark CPU score of 69,028.35, and 192.27 GB/sec uncached large-block memory read bandwidth. Although persistent storage must be attached externally via network volumes, the high memory-to-core ratio maximizes resource efficiency for memory-heavy deployments. The r8i.12xlarge is specifically designed for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caches, intensive data analytics, and CPU-based matrix inference workloads.
